title: Prove the peak-four cost of three-source XOR fanout
body:
For every n>=2, adding three restored helpers' parity to n dirty targets needs exactly 2n+2 unit XORs when the all-ones positive envelope is at most four. The structural lower bound allows arbitrary target feedback and any finite number of additional dirty auxiliaries. The attaining word reaches four in both directions.

This generalizes PR1520's three-target construction and replaces its finite shortest-word argument for this particular envelope floor with a uniform monotone-row proof. It does not repeat PR1557's unconstrained seven-register census. No clean roles, COPY/ERASE, frame changes or nonmonotone bounds are included; no new supplier or kappa is claimed.

Validation: registered Python3.12 replay passes 22 target/auxiliary cases in both directions; independent column replay and 15,680 complete dirty inputs; eight primary controls; Git-free empty-PATH export unchanged; both checkers reject three altered certificate fields. Independent agent proof review found no issue. The uniform lower bound is a prose proof, not a formal-kernel claim.
